task_2.title: Expose NothingType for attrs.NOTHING annotations
task_2.description: Version 24.3.0 adds a public type annotation alias for the existing attrs sentinel used to represent an omitted value when None is meaningful. This lets users type APIs that accept or return attrs.NOTHING consistently through the public attr and attrs packages without changing runtime sentinel behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can annotate APIs that accept or return the attrs omitted-value sentinel consistently by using a public NothingType that corresponds to attrs.NOTHING.

expectation.grounded: The upgrade should expose a public `NothingType` from both `attr` and `attrs`. `NothingType` must represent the same singleton sentinel exposed as `NOTHING`, so third-party code can use it in type annotations for parameters, defaults, and return values that may be `attrs.NOTHING`. The existing `NOTHING` sentinel remains the runtime value for omitted-state semantics.
expectation.conceptual: Applications should be able to rely on a supported public type for the attrs 'no value supplied' sentinel. Developers should be able to import that type from the main public packages and use it to document and type-check APIs that work with the sentinel.

constraints.grounded: This is an additive public API change. `NOTHING` must continue to behave as the existing sentinel, and code already using `attr.NOTHING` or `attrs.NOTHING` must keep working unchanged. The new type should describe only the sentinel value rather than broaden accepted runtime values.
constraints.conceptual: The update should add typing support without altering how omitted values behave at runtime. Existing sentinel-based code paths should remain compatible and keep the same observable behavior.

behavior: `NothingType` is publicly importable from `attr`.
`NothingType` is publicly importable from `attrs`.
`NothingType` denotes the singleton `NOTHING` sentinel used for the 'no value supplied' case.
Documentation for `NOTHING` should direct users to `NothingType` when they need to annotate third-party code that uses the sentinel.
acceptance_criteria: When a user imports from `attr`, `NothingType` should be available as a public symbol alongside `NOTHING`.
When a user imports from `attrs`, `NothingType` should be available as a public symbol alongside `NOTHING`.
When an API contract needs to express that a value may be the attrs omitted-value sentinel, it should be possible to annotate that contract with `NothingType`.
When existing code continues to use `NOTHING` at runtime, its omitted-value semantics should remain unchanged after the upgrade.

task_1.title: Drop Python 3.7 support in attrs 24.3.0
task_1.description: The 24.3.0 release raises the minimum supported Python version to 3.8 and removes Python 3.7 compatibility paths. On supported runtimes, attrs continues to rely on standard-library cached properties, typing protocols, and package metadata behavior without older fallback shims.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 24.3.0 is treated as a Python-version support change: Python 3.7 is no longer a supported runtime, while supported Python 3.8+ environments must retain existing attrs behavior for slotted classes, cached properties, typing protocols, and package metadata access.

expectation.grounded: attrs 24.3.0 should be consumed only on Python 3.8 or newer. On supported runtimes, importing and using `attr` or `attrs` should continue to work with standard-library `functools.cached_property` on slotted attrs classes, standard-library `typing.Protocol` and related typing primitives, and standard-library `importlib.metadata` for package metadata access.
expectation.conceptual: The upgrade should be understood as ending Python 3.7 compatibility while preserving normal library behavior for users already on supported Python versions. Supported environments should keep seeing the same public attrs capabilities through the standard Python 3.8+ library surface.

constraints.grounded: Do not broaden support back to Python 3.7 or require legacy compatibility packages for supported runtimes. Aside from the dropped interpreter floor, observable attrs behavior on Python 3.8+ should remain stable, including cached-property handling on slotted classes and normal package import and metadata behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the change scoped to the supported-Python baseline. Users on supported Python versions should not lose existing runtime functionality or need extra compatibility shims because of this upgrade.

behavior: attrs 24.3.0 treats Python 3.8 as the minimum supported interpreter and no longer maintains Python 3.7 compatibility branches.

On supported runtimes, attrs always assumes availability of standard-library `functools.cached_property`, so slotted attrs classes continue to interoperate with cached properties without version-gated behavior.
Package metadata access associated with the `attr` and `attrs` packages now relies on standard-library `importlib.metadata` rather than a Python 3.7 backport path.
Typing interoperability for attrs on supported runtimes aligns with standard-library `typing` features such as `Protocol` instead of older fallback imports.
acceptance_criteria: Given an application environment still running Python 3.7, when evaluating attrs 24.3.0, then that environment should be treated as unsupported for the upgrade.
Given Python 3.8 or newer, when importing and using `attr` or `attrs`, then normal package functionality should remain available without depending on legacy metadata or typing backport modules.
When a slotted attrs class defines a `functools.cached_property` on a supported runtime, it should continue to behave as a supported cached property on that class.
When attrs types are used alongside protocol-based typing on a supported runtime, the behavior should align with the standard-library `typing.Protocol` model.

task_3.title: Allow exception metadata updates on frozen attrs exceptions
task_3.description: The 24.3.0 update fixes frozen attrs-based exceptions so Python exception bookkeeping can still update note and context metadata without breaking immutability for normal attributes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that frozen attrs classes which inherit from BaseException continue to behave like normal Python exceptions when exception metadata is updated, including support for note and suppressed-context state, while remaining frozen for ordinary attribute changes.

expectation.grounded: For frozen attrs instances that are also BaseException subclasses, the generated frozen attribute guards must allow BaseException metadata updates for __suppress_context__ and __notes__ in the same way exception state already permits __cause__, __context__, and __traceback__. Deleting __notes__ on such frozen exception instances must also be allowed. These operations must not raise attr.exceptions.FrozenInstanceError.
expectation.conceptual: Frozen exceptions should still support the standard Python exception state that the runtime and application code may attach to raised exceptions. Updating or clearing exception notes or suppressed-context state should work normally instead of being blocked by the class being frozen.

constraints.grounded: The relaxation applies only to exception-specific BaseException metadata on frozen attrs exceptions. Attempts to set or delete unrelated attributes on frozen instances must continue to raise FrozenInstanceError, and non-exception frozen attrs classes must not gain broader mutability.
constraints.conceptual: This change must unblock normal exception bookkeeping without weakening the general immutability contract of frozen objects.

behavior: Assigning to __suppress_context__ on a frozen attrs exception succeeds instead of failing with FrozenInstanceError.
Assigning to __notes__ on a frozen attrs exception succeeds instead of failing with FrozenInstanceError.
Deleting __notes__ on a frozen attrs exception succeeds instead of failing with FrozenInstanceError.
Existing support for mutating other exception bookkeeping fields on frozen attrs exceptions remains intact.
Setting or deleting non-exception attributes on frozen attrs instances continues to be rejected.
acceptance_criteria: When a frozen attrs-based exception instance has its __suppress_context__ flag updated, it should accept the change without raising FrozenInstanceError.
When a frozen attrs-based exception instance has exception notes assigned or cleared through normal exception state manipulation, it should succeed without raising FrozenInstanceError.
When Python runtime behavior or user code updates exception chaining-related state on a frozen attrs-based exception, the exception should remain usable as a normal exception object.
When code attempts to mutate an ordinary field on a frozen attrs instance, it should still be rejected as a frozen-object violation.

task_4.title: Restore optional() compatibility with pipe() and Converter inputs
task_4.description: The attrs 24.3.0 update fixes converter composition so attrs.converters.optional() can wrap attrs.converters.pipe() and other Converter-based converters correctly. It also makes attrs.converters.pipe() preserve whether instance and field context is required, returning a plain callable for simple converter chains and a Converter only when context-aware converters are present.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that converter composition remains compatible when using attrs.converters.optional() with attrs.converters.pipe() or any other Converter-based converter, so optional conversion still short-circuits None values and otherwise applies the wrapped conversion chain correctly.

expectation.grounded: attrs.converters.optional() must accept either a regular callable converter or an attr.Converter input. When wrapping a Converter, the returned converter must preserve self/field-aware invocation and pass instance and attribute metadata through to the wrapped converter. attrs.converters.pipe() must return a regular callable when all supplied converters are plain callables, and it must return a Converter only when at least one supplied converter is an attr.Converter that requires instance/field context. In both APIs, None handling and chained conversion behavior must remain consistent with the wrapped converter's public behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Optional and piped converters should compose transparently. Wrapping a converter with optional behavior must still return None unchanged, and any non-None value must be processed through the wrapped converter or converter chain with the same externally observable behavior and context support as before.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing attrs.converters.optional() behavior for plain callable converters. Do not make attrs.converters.pipe() require instance/field context for converter chains that only contain plain callables. Preserve the public return contract that None bypasses conversion in optional(), and preserve chained conversion order in pipe().
constraints.conceptual: Existing simple converter usage should keep working unchanged. Context-aware conversion should only be enabled when the wrapped converter actually depends on attribute metadata, and composed converters should not alter ordering or the special handling of None values.

behavior: attrs.converters.optional() now supports wrapping attr.Converter instances in addition to plain callables.
When optional() wraps a Converter, non-None inputs are forwarded with the same instance and field context that the wrapped Converter expects.
attrs.converters.optional() still returns None unchanged without invoking the wrapped converter when the input value is None.
attrs.converters.pipe() now returns a plain callable for converter chains made only of plain callables.
attrs.converters.pipe() returns an attr.Converter when any converter in the chain is an attr.Converter, preserving instance/field-aware conversion across the full chain.
pipe() continues to apply converters in order, feeding each step's output into the next step.
acceptance_criteria: When attrs.converters.optional() wraps attrs.converters.pipe(...), passing None should yield None and passing a non-None value should apply the full pipeline successfully.
When attrs.converters.optional() wraps an attr.Converter, non-None inputs should be converted successfully instead of failing due to missing converter context.
When attrs.converters.pipe() is built only from plain callable converters, it should behave as a normal single-argument converter from the caller's perspective.
When attrs.converters.pipe() includes at least one attr.Converter, the composed converter should preserve instance/field-aware behavior and still run all converters in order.
Existing uses of optional() and pipe() with ordinary callable converters should continue to behave the same for successful conversions and error propagation.

task_6.title: Allow union types in attrs.validators.instance_of type hints
task_6.description: Version 24.3.0 expands the typed API for attrs.validators.instance_of() so users can declare accepted types with native union syntax such as str | int. Based on the provided materials, this is a typing compatibility improvement rather than a runtime validation change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs.validators.instance_of() supports union-type declarations in user code so developers can express multiple accepted types with native union syntax without changing the validator's observable runtime contract.

expectation.grounded: The public type hints for attrs.validators.instance_of() should accept union type expressions, including PEP 604 unions such as str | int and equivalent multi-type unions, as valid arguments to the validator factory. Existing instance_of usage with a single type or a tuple of types should remain valid, and no runtime validation change is evidenced by the provided production diff.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to configure instance_of() with normal Python union syntax when they want a validator to allow more than one type. This should improve typing compatibility while keeping validation behavior consistent with prior multi-type usage.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing attrs.validators.instance_of() support for single concrete types or tuple-based multi-type declarations. Do not introduce new validation outcomes, warning behavior, or error categories beyond widening typing acceptance for union-typed arguments.
constraints.conceptual: Existing code that already uses instance_of() should continue to work the same way. The change should broaden how accepted types can be declared in typed code, not alter what the validator does at runtime.

behavior: attrs.validators.instance_of() should accept union type expressions in its typed public API.
Union declarations with more than two member types should be supported the same way as simpler unions.
Existing single-type and tuple-of-types instance_of() declarations should remain supported.
No runtime behavior change is demonstrated by the provided production diff; the upgrade is limited to typing compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: When a developer calls attrs.validators.instance_of() with a PEP 604 union such as str | int, the API should be valid from a typing perspective.
When a developer passes a union containing multiple member types to attrs.validators.instance_of(), the declaration should be accepted consistently.
When existing code calls attrs.validators.instance_of() with one type or a tuple of types, it should continue to be accepted without behavioral regression.
When instance_of() is declared with union syntax, its runtime validation behavior should remain aligned with the library's existing multi-type instance checking semantics.

task_5.title: Support copy.replace() for attrs instances on Python 3.13+
task_5.description: The update adds native participation in Python 3.13's copy.replace() protocol for attrs-defined instances by automatically providing replacement behavior that matches attrs.evolve, while preserving any user-defined __replace__ implementation. It also adjusts frozen attrs exceptions so Python-managed exception metadata remains writable without making frozen instances generally mutable.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs-defined instances can be copied with field updates through Python 3.13's copy.replace() API, with behavior consistent with attrs.evolve, without overriding custom replacement hooks or weakening frozen-instance protections.

expectation.grounded: On Python 3.13 and later, classes generated by attrs should expose copy.replace() support by providing a __replace__ method unless the class already defines its own __replace__. The generated replacement behavior should follow attr.evolve semantics: accepted changes are keyed by the class's init-facing names, unspecified init=True attributes are copied from the source instance, and the new instance is produced through normal class construction. Invalid replacement names should continue to fail with a TypeError rather than being ignored. Frozen attrs classes should still raise FrozenInstanceError for ordinary attribute mutation, while frozen BaseException subclasses must allow Python-managed exception state such as cause, context, traceback, suppress-context, and notes metadata to be updated as needed.
expectation.conceptual: Users running Python 3.13+ should be able to call copy.replace() on attrs instances to create modified copies in the same way they already can with attrs.evolve. Existing custom replacement behavior must remain authoritative, unsupported field names must still fail loudly, and frozen attrs exceptions must stay frozen except for interpreter-managed exception bookkeeping.

constraints.grounded: Do not replace a class-defined __replace__. Only provide the automatic replacement hook where Python 3.13+ replacement support exists. Preserve current values for all init-participating attributes not explicitly changed, and do not treat non-init attributes as replaceable inputs. Keep existing attrs error behavior for invalid arguments and non-attrs usage. For frozen instances, continue rejecting normal set and delete operations with FrozenInstanceError; only the BaseException metadata attributes required for exception handling are exempt from that restriction.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must be additive and compatibility-safe: it should enable the new standard-library replacement workflow without changing existing custom APIs, without silently accepting unsupported field updates, and without making frozen objects broadly mutable.

behavior: Attrs-generated classes automatically participate in Python 3.13's copy.replace() protocol unless they already supply their own __replace__ method.
The default replacement path mirrors attrs.evolve by carrying forward unchanged init-enabled field values from the original instance and applying only the requested updates to the new instance.
Replacement requests that use names not accepted by the attrs class constructor fail with a TypeError instead of being ignored.
Frozen attrs instances remain protected against ordinary attribute assignment and deletion through FrozenInstanceError.
Frozen attrs classes that inherit from BaseException allow Python-managed exception metadata fields, including notes-related state, to be set or cleared as required for exception handling.
acceptance_criteria: Given an attrs instance on Python 3.13+, when copy.replace() is called with one or more valid init field names, then it should return a new instance of the same class with the requested fields changed and other init fields preserved from the original.
Given an attrs class that already defines __replace__, when the class is created, then attrs should leave that implementation unchanged rather than injecting its own replacement behavior.
Given a copy.replace() call for an attrs instance with a field name that is not accepted by the class constructor, when the replacement is attempted, then the operation should raise a TypeError.
Given a frozen attrs instance, when regular attributes are assigned or deleted, then the operation should still fail with FrozenInstanceError.

Given a frozen attrs exception instance, when Python updates or clears exception bookkeeping metadata such as notes or context-related state, then those metadata operations should succeed without making other attributes writable.
